name: Intel Gaudi 2
memory_bandwidth_basis: Vendor-published per-accelerator figure from the Gaudi 3 technical paper's Gaudi 2 vs Gaudi 3 comparison table: 96 GB HBM2e at 2.46 TB/s.

flops.notes: BF16 VECTOR path (scalar ALUs), not the MME matrix path. Recorded as its own row with a distinct unit because Gaudi quotes 432 MME BF16 TFLOPS and 112 BF16 vector TFLOPS on the same part; they are different quantities and must not be compared or summed. MME is the tensor-core path that runs matrix work; the vector path is what runs elementwise and reduction work.

notes:
Numbers are taken from the Gaudi 3 technical paper's comparison table, since Intel never published a standalone Gaudi 2 datasheet that is reachable; treat them as vendor-published but second-hand. The third flops row is BF16 VECTOR TFLOPS (112), a different unit to the first two (MME TFLOPS 432) and therefore NOT a contradiction - it is recorded as its own flops row with unit 'bf16-vector-tflops' so the two quantities are never compared or summed. CORRECTED 2026-10-04: the notes previously claimed this row existed in the flops array when it did not - only the 432 MME and 865 FP8 rows were present.. On-die SRAM is 48 MB at 6.4/6.4 TB/s, half of Gaudi 3. 2 MME units and 24 TPC units. 600 GB/s bidirectional networking versus Gaudi 3's 1200. Host interface is PCIe Gen4 x16 at 64 GB/s peak versus Gaudi 3's PCIe Gen5 at 128. AUDIT 2026-10-04 (PCIE PER-DIRECTION VERIFIED, no value changed): Intel's Gaudi 3 technical paper Table 1 prints the host link with an explicit direction split that removes all ambiguity - 'Host Interface Peak BW | 64 GB/s (32 GB/s per direction) | 128 GB/s (64 GB/s per direction)' for Gaudi 2 and Gaudi 3 respectively. So Intel's own 'peak BW' figure is the BIDIRECTIONAL AGGREGATE and the per-direction number is half of it. 32 GB/s per direction on Gen4 x16 is exactly 16 GT/s x 16 lanes / 8 = 32 GB/s, confirming the convention. The 64 GB/s in this record is therefore already the aggregate and must NOT be halved again - this is the specific double-halving failure mode flagged for this repo, and Intel publishing both numbers in the same table cell is what makes it preventable. Nothing in this record stores a per-direction PCIe figure, so no numeric field changed; the annotation exists so a future reader does not 'fix' a number that is already right. Included as a separate record because it remains in cloud and OEM fleets and because the architectural delta (SRAM tier, MME/TPC split, die count) is what makes the Gaudi 3 comparison meaningful. Still shipping in Intel's own and OEM racks and on IBM Cloud / AWS DL1.

POWER: tdp_w was null with a note asserting 'TDP is not published in the technical paper'. That is FALSE. Intel publishes it twice in the Gaudi 3 technical paper: Table 8 gives '600 W | 900 W' for Gaudi 2 OAM vs Gaudi 3 OAM, and the prose gives 'up to 900W Total Device Power' for the HL-325L OAM. 600 W is the Gaudi 2 OAM (HL-225 OAM) figure. The single tdp_w field cannot hold both form factors, so it holds the OAM value and the alternative is named here.
